    83	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    84	
    85	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    86	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    88	-/
    89	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    90	
    91	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    93	-/
    94	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    95	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    96	
    97	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    99	-/
   100	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   101	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   102	
   103	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   105	-/
   106	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   107	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   108	
   109	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   110	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   111	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   112	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   115	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   116	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   117	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   118	
   119	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   120	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   121	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   122	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   124	-/
   125	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   126	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   127	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   128	
   129	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   130	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   131	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   133	-/
   134	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   135	  fun i => match i with
   136	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   137	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   138	  | .inr _ => 0
   139	
   140	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   141	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   142	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   143	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   144	-/
   145	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   146	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   147	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   148	  fun i => match i with
   149	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   150	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   151	  | .inr _ => 0
   152	
   153	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   154	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   155	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   156	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   158	-/
   159	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   160	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   161	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   162	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   163	  fun i => match i with
   164	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   165	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   166	  | .inr j => direction j
   167	
   168	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   169	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   170	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   172	-/
   173	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   174	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   175	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   176	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   177	
   178	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the shared scalar
   179	coordinate of the ambient low-degree space.  It is the first register in the
   180	concatenation exhibiting the conditional-linearity levels asserted in
   181	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint

   184	private def ldSeedRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   185	  {Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())}
   186	
   187	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the point coordinates
   188	of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   189	private def ldPointRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   190	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j) : LdIndex P)

   192	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the direction
   193	coordinates of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   194	private def ldDirectionRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   195	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inr j : LdIndex P)

   197	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map retaining the shared scalar
   198	coordinate and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   199	private def ldSeedLinear (P : LdParams) :
   200	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   201	  toFun x := fun i =>
   202	    match i with
   203	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   204	    | .inl (.inr _) => x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   205	    | .inr _ => 0
   206	  map_add' x y := by
   207	    funext i
   208	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   209	  map_smul' c x := by
   210	    funext i
   211	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp

   213	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map sending the point block to its
   214	canonical line representative in the fixed direction `v` and clearing every
   215	other coordinate. -/
   216	private noncomputable def ldPointCLLinear (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   217	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   218	  toFun x := fun i =>
   219	    match i with
   220	    | .inl (.inl j) => lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point x) j
   221	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   222	    | .inr _ => 0
   223	  map_add' x y := by
   224	    funext i
   225	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   226	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (x + y)) j = _
   227	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (x + y) = LdSpace.point x + LdSpace.point y := rfl
   228	      rw [hpoint, map_add]
   229	      rfl
   230	    · simp
   231	    · simp
   232	  map_smul' c x := by
   233	    funext i
   234	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   235	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (c • x)) j = _
   236	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl
   237	      rw [hpoint, map_smul]
   238	      rfl
   239	    · simp
   240	    · simp

   248	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   249	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   250	    | .inr j => prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j

   295	      (lineRepMap
   296	        (prefixProjection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z))
   297	          (prefixProjection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)) (LdSpace.direction z)))
   298	        (lineRepMap
   299	          (prefixProjection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)) (LdSpace.direction z))

   301	      (prefixProjection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z))

   322	/-- The low-degree question sampler equals the distribution that the
   323	construction of `def:typed-cl-distributions` (`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1400-1404`)
   324	produces from the family `ldCL` on the complete type graph. This is the

   326	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`; the assertion that `ldCL` is a typed family of

   328	open obligation is tracked by issue #180. Paper
   329	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
   330	theorem ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL (L : LdParams) :
   331	    ldQuestionDistribution L =
   332	      typedCLDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) (by simp)
   333	        (ldCL L) (ldCL L) := by
   334	  have hgraph : ∀ hE : (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)).Nonempty,
   335	      graphDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) hE =
   336	        uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType) := by
   337	    intro hE
   338	    have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (LdType × LdType)).filter
   339	        fun ab => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)))
   340	        = (Finset.univ : Finset (LdType × LdType)) := by
   341	      simp
   342	    change Distribution.uniformOnFinset _ = _
   343	    rw [hfilter]
   344	    rfl
   345	  have hleft : ldQuestionDistribution L =
   346	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType))
   347	        (fun uv => (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   348	          fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z))) := by
   349	    rw [bind_uniformDistribution_map]

   355	            fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z))) := by
   356	    intro hE
   357	    have hfamily : (fun uv : LdType × LdType =>

   361	        fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z)) := by
   362	      funext uv
   363	      exact Distribution.map_map _ _ _
   364	    change Distribution.bind (graphDistribution _ hE) _ = _
   365	    rw [hgraph hE, hfamily]

     3	/-!
     4	# Finite-field bases and the fixed binary representation
     5	
     6	The Pauli basis test uses fields of size `2^k` for odd `k`, together with a
     7	chosen self-dual normal basis over `ZMod 2`.  This file constructs such bases
     8	and records the resulting fixed field model for later proofs.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The declarations correspond to `def:admissible-size`,
    13	`def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis`, `def:subfields-kappa`, `def:subfield-trace`,
    14	and `def:binary-representation` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:182-257` and `298-315`.
    16	Their paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502,653-728`.
    17	-/

    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	/-- `IsAdmissibleSize q` is the predicate `q = 2^k` for an odd exponent.
    24	This is `def:admissible-size` in the blueprint
    25	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:210-212`, with paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:662-667`.
    27	-/
    28	def IsAdmissibleSize (q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ k : ℕ, Odd k ∧ q = 2 ^ k
    29	
    30	/-- A dual pair of bases for `def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis`, blueprint
    31	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:241-257`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:494-496`. -/
    32	def IsDualBasisPair {F K ι : Type*} [CommRing F] [CommRing K] [DecidableEq ι]
    33	    [Algebra F K] (b b' : Module.Basis ι F K) : Prop :=
    34	  ∀ i j, Algebra.trace F K (b i * b' j) = if i = j then 1 else 0
    35	
    36	namespace Basis

    38	/-- Self-duality in `def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis`, blueprint
    39	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:241-257`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:494-497`. -/
    40	def IsSelfDual {F K ι : Type*} [CommRing F] [CommRing K] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    [Algebra F K] (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : Prop :=
    42	  IsDualBasisPair b b
    43	
    44	/-- Normality in `def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis`, blueprint
    45	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:241-257`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:498-502`. The
    46	Frobenius exponent uses the cardinality of the base field. -/
    47	def IsNormal {F K : Type*} [CommSemiring F] [Fintype F] [Field K] [Algebra F K]
    48	    {k : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin k) F K) : Prop :=
    49	  ∃ α : K, ∀ j, b j = α ^ (Fintype.card F ^ j.1)

    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint

    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool

    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and

    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=

    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by

    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.

    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=

  1351	\label{sec:types}
  1352	
  1353	The question distribution of the Pauli basis test is \emph{typed}: each question is a pair consisting of a type, drawn together with the other player's type from the edges of a fixed \emph{type graph}, and a question content, drawn from a CL distribution determined by the pair of types.

Finiteness of $\mathcal T$ plays no part in this definition, which is therefore stated, as in the linked declaration, for an arbitrary type set; it is required from Definition~\ref{def:graph-distribution} onwards, where $\mathcal T$ indexes a distribution. The source states the definition for a finite type set, and every type set occurring below is finite.

Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of $G$} is the distribution over $U \times U$ such that for every $(u,v) \in U \times U$,
  1369		\[
  1370			\mu_G(u, v) =
  1371			\begin{cases}

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions
     5	
     6	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
     7	graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
     8	map to that seed.  A conditionally linear map of level `ell` is a sum of `ell`
     9	linear contributions on pairwise disjoint register subspaces, each contribution
    10	selected by the values of the preceding ones; the predicate below records that
    11	decomposition, and the graph distribution is the law of the type pair.  Direct
    12	sums of conditionally linear maps over pairwise disjoint registers are
    13	established in
    14	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/CondLinearTheorems/DirectSumSupport.lean`.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`
    19	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`), `def:cl-dist`
    20	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1199-1202`), `lem:cl-concat`
    21	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1235-1249`), and `def:graph-distribution`
    22	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1365-1377`).
    23	The paper origins are
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57,282-314`,
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`,
    26	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
    27	-/
    28	
    29	open scoped BigOperators
    30	
    31	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    32	
    33	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    34	
    35	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	
    37	/--
    38	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    39	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    40	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    41	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    42	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    43	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    44	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`,
    45	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    46	-/
    47	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    48	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    49	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    50	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    51	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    52	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    53	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    54	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    55	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    56	
    57	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    58	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    59	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    61	-/
    62	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    63	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    64	
    65	/-- Evaluation of a representation of a conditionally linear function.
    66	Lean-only support for `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    67	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    68	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    69	-/
    70	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    71	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    72	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    73	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    74	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    75	      fun x =>
    76	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    77	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    78	
    79	/-- The support invariant for a representation of a conditionally linear
    80	function.  This is a Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    83	-/
    84	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    85	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    86	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    87	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    88	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    89	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    90	
    91	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    92	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    93	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    94	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    95	-/
    96	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    97	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    98	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    99	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
   100	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L

    26	### The rule
    27	
    28	A declaration presented as the formalization of a paper theorem, lemma,
    29	proposition, or corollary must state the paper result, up to faithful formal
    30	encoding of the mathematical domain.  Its public hypotheses and conclusion are
    31	both part of the statement.  Adding a load-bearing bridge, residual, repair,
    32	obligation-structure input, hypotheses bundle, or assumptions bundle not present
    33	in the cited statement changes the theorem into a conditional helper.
    34	
    35	The project therefore distinguishes three objects.
    36	
    37	| Object | Public statement | Blueprint status |
    38	|--------|------------------|------------------|
    39	| Paper theorem | Matches the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/` | May be linked by source-labelled `\lean{}`; statement-level `\leanok` only when the statement matches |
    40	| Internal proof obligation | Proves a missing intermediate mathematical input from paper hypotheses | May contain a tracked `sorry` while the proof is open |
    41	| Conditional helper | Quarantines an unproved intermediate obligation | Not a paper theorem; no source-labelled `\leanok` |
    42	
    43	It is never allowed to change the public statement of a declaration presented
    44	as the formalization of a source-labelled paper theorem.  At the final assembly
    45	point, the paper theorem must either discharge the extra hypotheses internally,
    46	or remain as the paper-aligned statement with an unfinished proof while the
    47	conditional helper is given a different name.
    48	
    49	The preferred way to expose unfinished work is a named internal theorem or
    50	definition with a precise paper-origin docstring and, if necessary, a tracked
    51	`sorry`.  This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement
    52	of a source-labelled theorem.
    53	
    54	### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily
    55	
    56	| Temporary reason | Explanation |
    57	|------------------|-------------|
    58	| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |
    59	| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |
    60	| **Auditability** | An explicit temporary hypothesis is easier to find than an implicit assumption hidden in prose, provided it is named as proof debt. |
    61	
    62	These reasons do not justify strengthening a paper theorem.  They only explain
    63	why a short-lived helper declaration may exist while its remaining hypotheses
    64	are being actively removed.
    65	
    66	### How to proceed when a proof needs an extra input
    67	
    68	1. **Check the source statement.**  Read the corresponding TeX in
    69	   `references/ldt-paper/` before changing a theorem linked from the blueprint.
    70	2. **Keep the paper-facing declaration source-faithful.**  Boundary hypotheses
    71	   such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances, or
    72	   type-class assumptions may be faithful encodings when they are needed to
    73	   state the mathematics in Lean.  Proof data such as `BridgeInputs`,
    74	   `RepairInput`, `Residual`, `Package`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic
    75	   `Assumptions` is different: it is not a paper assumption unless the cited
    76	   statement says so.
    77	3. **Name the missing intermediate result.**  If the proof uses a mathematical
    78	   fact not yet formalized, state it as a separate proof obligation.  A
    79	   temporary `sorry` in this declaration is preferable to adding the obligation as
    80	   a hypothesis on the paper theorem.
    81	4. **Do not introduce conditional helpers by default.**  A helper whose name
    82	   ends in `_ofObligations` is a quarantine device, not a normal formalization
    83	   pattern.  It may remain temporarily only when it preserves substantial proof
    84	   content that cannot yet be connected to the paper hypotheses, has a tracked
    85	   discharge or deletion target, and has no source-labelled blueprint
    86	   `\leanok`.  If the helper would merely package missing work as an extra
    87	   hypothesis, restore the theorem with the paper statement and leave a tracked
    88	   `sorry` instead.
    89	5. **Audit the final statement.**  Every PR touching a source-labelled theorem
    90	   should compare paper assumptions and Lean assumptions, paper conclusion and
    91	   Lean conclusion, and report whether the Lean statement is exact, has only
    92	   faithful boundary hypotheses, or has extra assumptions.
    93	
    94	If a paper-facing declaration is temporarily proved by calling a conditional
    95	helper whose load-bearing input has not yet been produced from the paper
    96	hypotheses, the proof frontier must be marked explicitly.  The declaration
    97	should carry an `**Unfaithful:**` docstring section naming the non-paper
    98	dependency, citing the paper-gap note or tracking issue, and identifying the
    99	internal theorem that will remove the dependency.  A named proof obligation
   100	with a tracked `sorry` is preferred whenever possible, because it makes the
   101	missing mathematical assertion visible without adding it to the paper theorem
   102	statement.
   103	
   104	### Required metadata for new proof-obligation declarations
   105	
   106	A new declaration whose name contains a proof-debt token such as `Bridge`,
   107	`Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Producer`, `Input`, `Hypotheses`,
   108	`Assumptions`, `Obligation`, or `Witness` must explain its mathematical role in
   109	the def-site docstring.  A paper citation alone is not enough, because the

1	# Blueprint Style Guide & Lessons Learned
     2	
     3	## Core Philosophy
     4	The blueprint is a **bridge between the mathematics and the Lean formalization**. A reader should be able to read a blueprint entry and immediately understand the corresponding Lean declaration. Conversely, someone reading the Lean code should find the blueprint proof sketch faithful to what the code actually does.
     5	
     6	## General Principles
     7	1. **Blueprint ↔ Lean must match.** Every `\lean{X}` tag must correspond to an actual Lean declaration. Every proof sketch must match what the Lean proof actually does — not a hand-wavy version of it.
     8	2. **Standalone.** `blueprint/` and any slides are independent — no cross-references, no shared files. Each has its own macros, its own `references.bib`.
     9	3. **Mathematical language only — zero Lean jargon.** No Lean identifiers in prose (no `selfImprovement_step`, no `PastingLemma.aux`, no `rintro ⟨X, hX⟩`). The `\lean{...}` tag is the link; the body text is standard mathematics. If you can't say it in math, rewrite it.
    10	4. **No filler prose.** Only precise definitions, theorem statements, and proof sketches. No "this is important because..." or "the self-improvement step governs the induction...".
    11	5. **Cite non-trivial things.** Basic definitions don't need citations. Important results and non-obvious definitions should cite the source paper.
    12	6. **Don't invent terminology or notation.** Don't create ad-hoc notation when standard notation exists. Don't name things that the literature doesn't name.
    13	7. **Match Lean's theorem/lemma/def exactly.** If Lean says `theorem X`, use `\begin{theorem}`. If Lean says `lemma X`, use `\begin{lemma}`. `\begin{proposition}` is allowed in blueprint prose when it improves mathematical readability, but still map it to an actual Lean `theorem`/`lemma` declaration via `\lean{...}`. Label prefix: `thm:` for theorem, `lem:` for lemma, `def:` for definition, `prop:` for proposition.
    14	
    15	### Remark On Mathematical Prose
    16	
    17	Blueprint entries should read as mathematical exposition, not as progress
    18	reports. The mathematical argument should determine the order of the prose:
    19	introduce the notation, state the assertion, give the proof or calculation, and
    20	then record Lean references through the usual blueprint tags. Lean declarations,
    21	file paths, and proof-status information should not become the visible structure
    22	of the paragraph. When referring to a source article, cite it bibliographically
    23	rather than relying on an uncited reference to the article.
    24	
    25	Use displayed formulae when the formula benefits from visual separation, and
    26	keep short scalar definitions or elementary inequalities inline when the
    27	sentence reads better that way. As in ordinary mathematical writing, displayed
    28	formulae should be punctuated as part of the sentences in which they occur.
    29	
    30	## Proof Sketches Must Match Lean
    31	This is the most important rule. Every proof in the blueprint must faithfully describe what the Lean proof does:
    32	
    33	- **Reference the actual lemmas used.** If the Lean proof calls `LDT.selfImprovement`, the blueprint proof should say "By Lemma X.Y (self-improvement)..." and list it in `\uses`.
    34	- **Do not use `\cref` or `\Cref`.** The blueprint does not load `cleveref`.
    35	  Spell out the kind of object and use ordinary references, for example
    36	  `Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement}` or `Theorem~\ref{thm:main-formal}`.
    37	- **Describe the actual proof structure.** If Lean does induction on a parameter, say so. If Lean uses a specific decomposition, name it.

    23	For every `\begin{theorem|lemma|proposition|corollary|definition}` block in

    25	records two independent flags based on `\leanok` placement (see

    30	- **proof-level** — `\leanok` inside the matching
    31	  `\begin{proof}…\end{proof}`, i.e. the Lean proof is claimed complete.

    33	A declaration may have both, only one, or neither. The axiom-closure check
    34	then classifies findings by the strongest placement observed:
    35	
    36	| Condition                                                                                | Severity |
    37	|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|
    38	| `Name` is not a known Lean declaration, and the block has **proof-level** `\leanok`       | error    |
    39	| `Name` is not a known Lean declaration, and the block has only **statement-level** `\leanok` | warning  |

    44	| Block has only **statement-level** `\leanok` and `#print axioms Name` output could not be parsed (fail-safe) | warning  |

    46	| `Name` is sorry-free but the block has no `\leanok` anywhere                              | warning  |

    49	`\leanok` only claims the Lean statement matches the blueprint; it is **not**

 The Pauli basis test is the quantum low individual degree test of Natarajan and Vidick, in the slightly modified form introduced by Natarajan and Wright~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Informally, the test certifies that the players share the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, where $M = 2^m$. On a question of type $(\mathsf{Pauli}, W)$ with $W \in \{X,Z\}$, a player is expected to measure the generalized Pauli basis POVM $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} and report the outcome $h$. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$. The two binary measurements obtained in this way for $W = X$ and $W = Z$ either commute or anticommute, according to the value $\gamma \in \F_2$ of Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value} below. When $\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.

# Mathematical Language Guidelines

MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
the formalization with the paper and blueprint.

This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.

## Scope

These guidelines apply to:

- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
- module docstrings;
- declaration docstrings;
- documentation-visible section comments;
- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
- issue titles and issue bodies;
- PR titles and PR descriptions.

## Source of Truth

Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:

1. `references/ldt-paper/`
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files

When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.

## Reference Notation And Terminology

The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.

When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
first applicable location in the following order:

1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
   differs from the paper;
2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
   family of declarations in that file;
3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
   blueprint;
4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.

The explanation should say:

- the notation or term used in the paper;
- the Lean object or name which represents it;
- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
- the scope in which the replacement should be used.

A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
where future readers can learn it.

Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.

## Naming Norm

Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled.

Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
clearer phrase.

This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
number, or implementation history.

### Concrete examples

The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
paper or blueprint would recognize.

| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |

An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.

File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.

### Shared helpers

When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

Procedure:

1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   explicit argument.
2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   blueprint location it supports.

### Legacy identifier treatment

If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.

Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.

## Review Checklist

Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.

- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
      implementation-phase labels)?
- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
      source does not use them that way?
- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
      that order of preference?
- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
      construction they support?
- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.

Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
relevant audit before changing names or prose.

docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:177:**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:179:**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. docs/formalization-patterns.md:3:Key design patterns used in the MIPStarRE Lean formalization to bridge the

The original reference controls notation whenever it gives a usable convention.
If the blueprint needs a different symbol, index convention, or name in order to
match Lean, introduce it explicitly and relate it to the paper notation in the
same paragraph.  Do not let a `\lean{...}` tag, a Lean namespace, or a file name
be the only explanation of a changed term.

When a public Lean declaration is a formalization-only auxiliary lemma, the
blueprint should say so before listing the declaration.  The surrounding prose
should identify the paper theorem, equation, or construction that the auxiliary
lemma supports, and should avoid making the auxiliary name look like a named
result from the source article.

## What NOT to Put in the Blueprint
- **Lean identifier names in math text.** Write "the self-improvement lemma", never "the `selfImprovement` step". The `\lean{LDT.selfImprovement}` tag handles the linking.
- **Implementation details.** Don't say "bundled as an element of the Euclidean space" or "using `EuclideanSpace.equiv`". Describe the mathematical object.
- **Ad-hoc notation.** Don't invent superscripts or subscripts to distinguish from existing notation. Use standard conventions.
- **Function-call syntax.** Use mathematical notation, not programming notation.
- **Redundant definitions.** If two blueprint definitions describe the same mathematical object, consolidate them. Each definition should introduce genuinely new mathematical content.
- **Lean namespace prefixes in prose.** Don't write "the `LDT.PastingLemma`" — write "the pasting lemma".

## Banned AI/Software Language (enforced in both blueprint AND Lean code)
The blueprint reads as a **mathematical document**, not software documentation. The following patterns are banned in ALL reader-facing text (section titles, theorem names, proof sketches, remarks, chapter preambles) and in ALL Lean docstrings, comments, and section names:

### Banned terms → replacements:
| Banned | Use instead |
|--------|------------|
| "Assembly" (as section/chapter title) | "Proof of [theorem]", "Construction", "Composition" |
| "Pipeline" | "reduction", "construction", "proof chain" |
| "Bridge" (as noun for a connection) | "connection", name by mathematical content |
| "Handoff" / "hand off" | "transition", "continuation", or drop entirely |
| "In this blueprint" / "Within this blueprint" | "here", "in what follows", or omit |
| "Honest" (as adjective for rigorous) | "exact", "faithful", "unconditional", "complete" |
| "Glue layer" | "intermediate construction", "connecting results" |
| "Re-export" / "reexport" | "provides", "re-states" |
| "Wiring" / "wire up" | "connecting", "composing", "combining" |
| "Package" (as noun for a data bundle) | "form", "data", "structure" |
| "Sorry-free" | acceptable only in Lean-specific technical context |

### Additional rules:
- **Section names in Lean**: use mathematical terms (`section QuantumSoundness`, `section SelfImprovement`, `section PastingLemma`), not organizational terms (`section Assembly`, `section Pipeline`).
- **Internal LaTeX labels** (e.g., `\label{ch:soundness}`) are not reader-facing and need not be renamed if doing so would break cross-references. But NEW labels should follow the standard.
- **Definitions that are actually theorems**: if a statement asserts a mathematical fact, it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not `\begin{definition}`. Definitions introduce new objects; theorems prove properties.

## `\uses` Dependency Guidelines
- **Statement `\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.
- **Proof `\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.
- **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.

## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
look as if the paper stated them.

- If a declaration directly formalizes a paper or blueprint statement, record
  it as usual with `\lean{...}` on that statement and cite the relevant source.
- If a public declaration is an auxiliary lemma introduced only for the Lean
  proof, make that status explicit. Its Lean docstring should say that it is a
  formalization-only auxiliary lemma and should name the nearby paper equation,
  line range, or blueprint result it supports.
- If such an auxiliary declaration is important enough to be referenced from
  the blueprint, give it a clearly subordinate blueprint node, for example
  `[Formalization support for ...]`, and state in the first sentence that the
  lemma is not a named statement of the paper but isolates a step used in the
  Lean proof.
- Connect auxiliary nodes to the corresponding result from the paper with `\uses{...}` from
  the proof that actually calls them. Do not add them only to silence a sync
  warning; the dependency edge should explain where the auxiliary result is
  used.
- Do not mark an auxiliary node with proof-level `\leanok` unless its Lean proof
  is complete and `#print axioms` has no `sorryAx`. Statement-level `\leanok`
  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the
  proof remains tracked as incomplete.

## Blueprint Structure
- `content.tex` is a router: `\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.
- Each chapter is a separate file in `chapter/`
- Definitions/theorems numbered within chapters: `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[chapter]`


## Lean Blueprint Macros
- `\lean{Namespace.DeclName}` — links to Lean declaration
- `\leanok` — context-sensitive marker; see "Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`" below
- `\uses{label1, label2}` — declares dependency edges for the graph
- `\notready` — marks as not ready for formalization (orange in graph)
- `\mathlibok` — already in Mathlib (dark green in graph; see legend note below)

### Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`

`\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The same macro is used for two different claims, so reviewers should read it by placement rather than by raw token count.

**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\leanok` marker.

**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).

A theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary node is **fully formalized in Lean if and only if it has both markers**: statement-level `\leanok` in the statement block and proof-level `\leanok` in the proof block. Statement-level without proof-level means “the statement has been transcribed and matched, but the proof is not yet certified complete.” Definitions have no proof block, so statement-level `\leanok` alone is enough there.

Excerpt from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`:

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Commutativity of the point measurements]\label{thm:commutativity-points}
  \lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.CommutativityPoints.commutativityPoints}
  \leanok
  \uses{def:good-strategy, def:approx_delta}
  Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  The strategy passes the diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma$.
\end{proof}
```

**Current CI behavior.** The advisory Blueprint ↔ Lean sync check in [`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`](ci-blueprint-sync.md) distinguishes the two placements. Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.

`leanblueprint` does not use distinct macro names for these two claims, so audits must distinguish them by environment context rather than by raw `\leanok` counts. A future split such as `\leanokstmt` / `\leanokproof` could make that distinction explicit, but that is only a possible later cleanup; the current convention is to keep `\leanok` and rely on placement.

A recurring historical example is the chapter 4 `Q/X/\widehat X/P` witness
layer.  Once Lean has construction theorems deriving the displayed identities
and estimates from the rank-reduction, sigma-range, positive-Gram, native
spectral-theorem, or rectangular-SVD hypotheses, the corresponding blueprint
entries may carry `\leanok`.  A declaration that merely projects an identity
from an opaque data record is not enough by itself, and a theorem depending on
extra rectangular-SVD data should not be used as evidence for an unconditional
paper statement unless a separate construction supplies that data.

## Dependency Graph Colors (web)
- **Light green box**: definition with `\lean` + `\leanok` (defined in Lean)
- **Green**: theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary with `\lean` + statement-level `\leanok` (statement matched in Lean)
- **Dark green**: either (i) theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary with both statement-level and proof-level `\leanok` (fully formalized in Lean), or (ii) a `\mathlibok` node
- **Blue**: ready to state/prove (all deps are done)
- **Orange**: `\notready` (needs more blueprint work)

   263	private theorem isCondLinearOn_one_of_linear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   264	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (L : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K)) :
   265	    IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ 1 (fun x => L x) := by
   266	  refine ⟨.succ Finset.univ L (fun _ i hi => absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) hi)

   268	  funext x
   269	  have hx : coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ : Finset ι) x = x := by
   270	    funext i
   271	    simp [coordinateRestriction]
   272	  show L (coordinateRestriction Finset.univ x) + 0 = L x
   273	  rw [hx, add_zero]

   275	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: extend a coefficient vector along an injective
   276	reindexing of registers, setting every coordinate outside the image to zero.
   277	The extension is used to reindex a conditionally linear map along `f`, with zero
   278	coordinates outside its image. This supports the transport of conditional
   279	linearity between the register spaces of `def:cl-func`,
   280	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`,
   281	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`. -/
   282	private def clExtend {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] (f : κ → ι) (u : κ → K) : ι → K :=
   283	  Function.extend f u 0
   284	
   285	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension recovers the original
   286	coordinates along an injective reindexing. -/
   287	private theorem clExtend_apply {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] {f : κ → ι}
   288	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u : κ → K) (k : κ) :
   289	    clExtend f u (f k) = u k :=
   290	  hf.extend_apply u 0 k
   291	
   292	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension vanishes at any coordinate
   293	outside the image of the reindexing. -/
   294	private theorem clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K]
   295	    (f : κ → ι) (u : κ → K) (i : ι) (h : ∀ k, f k ≠ i) :
   296	    clExtend f u i = 0 :=
   297	  Function.extend_apply' u (0 : ι → K) i
   298	    (fun hex => h hex.choose hex.choose_spec)
   299	
   300	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: restriction along an injective reindexing
   301	inverts the extension. -/
   302	private theorem clExtend_comp {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] {f : κ → ι}
   303	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u : κ → K) :
   304	    (fun k => clExtend f u (f k)) = u :=
   305	  funext fun k => clExtend_apply hf u k
   306	
   307	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension of the zero vector vanishes. -/
   308	private theorem clExtend_zero {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] {f : κ → ι}
   309	    (hf : Function.Injective f) : clExtend f (0 : κ → K) = 0 := by
   310	  funext i
   311	  by_cases h : ∃ k, f k = i
   312	  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h
   313	    simp [clExtend_apply hf]
   314	  · simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ h]
   315	
   316	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension is additive. -/
   317	private theorem clExtend_add {K κ ι : Type*} [AddZeroClass K] {f : κ → ι}
   318	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u v : κ → K) :
   319	    clExtend f (u + v) = clExtend f u + clExtend f v := by
   320	  funext i
   321	  by_cases h : ∃ k, f k = i
   322	  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h
   323	    simp [clExtend_apply hf]
   324	  · simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ h]
   325	
   326	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension commutes with scalars. -/
   327	private theorem clExtend_smul {K κ ι : Type*} [Semiring K] {f : κ → ι}
   328	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (c : K) (u : κ → K) :
   329	    clExtend f (c • u) = c • clExtend f u := by
   330	  funext i
   331	  by_cases h : ∃ k, f k = i
   332	  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h
   333	    simp [clExtend_apply hf]
   334	  · simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ h]

   336	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a linear map of coefficient vectors
   337	along an injective reindexing of registers; see `clExtend`.  Supports
   338	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`,

   340	private def clReindexLinear {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] {f : κ → ι}
   450	    (hf : Function.Injective f) {ell : ℕ} {L : (κ → K) → (κ → K)}
   451	    (h : IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L) :
   452	    IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell
   453	      (fun x => clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))) := by
   454	  obtain ⟨t, hsupp, hval⟩ := h
   455	  refine ⟨clReindexTerm hf t,
   456	    clReindexTerm_supportedOn hf t Finset.univ Finset.univ hsupp
   457	      (Finset.subset_univ _), ?_⟩
   458	  funext x
   459	  rw [clReindexTerm_eval hf t x, hval]

   516	    Function.Injective (pauliLdIndex P W) := by

   526	    (z : PauliSpace P) :

   528	  funext k

   531	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: writing a low-degree vector into the ambient
   532	Pauli registers is extension along `pauliLdIndex`; see

   535	private theorem embedLd_eq (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   536	    (w : LdSpace P.toLdParams) :
   537	    embedLd P W w = clExtend (pauliLdIndex P W) w := by
   538	  have hf := pauliLdIndex_injective P W

   541	  · cases W
   542	    · exact (clExtend_apply hf w (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j))).symm
   543	    · exact (clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem _ w _ (by
   544	        rintro ((j' | u') | j') <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
   545	  · cases W
   546	    · exact (clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem _ w _ (by
   547	        rintro ((j' | u') | j') <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
   548	    · exact (clExtend_apply hf w (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j))).symm
   549	  · exact (clExtend_apply hf w (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))).symm
   550	  · exact (clExtend_apply hf w (Sum.inr j)).symm
   551	  · exact (clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem _ w _ (by
   552	      intro k
   553	      cases W <;> rcases k with (j' | u') | j' <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
   554	  · exact (clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem _ w _ (by
   555	      intro k
   556	      cases W <;> rcases k with (j' | u') | j' <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm

   565	    (fun z : PauliSpace P => embedLd P W (L (pauliToLd P W z))) =

   567	        (L (fun k => z (pauliLdIndex P W k))) := by
   568	  funext z

   571	/-- Level assertions for the typed Pauli CL maps.  These are Lean-only
   572	proof obligations corresponding to the prose following `def:pauli-question-distribution`
   573	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:350-398`; paper
   574	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).

   576	`lem:pauli-question-typed-cl`; promotion to one common level is tracked by issue #180.

   578	theorem isCondLinear_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :

   581	      (pauliSharedProjection (P := P)) :=
   582	    isCondLinearOn_one_of_linear (pauliSharedProjectionLinear P)

   586	        (fun z : PauliSpace P =>

   593	        (fun z : PauliSpace P =>

   607	  | pair => exact hshared

   610	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   611	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   612	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:350-398`, paper origin
   613	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   614	-/
   615	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   616	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   617	  let lineEdges :=
   618	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   619	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   620	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   621	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   622	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   623	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   624	  let basisEdges :=
   625	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   626	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   627	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   628	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   629	  let pairEdges :=
   630	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   631	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   632	  let msEdges' :=
   633	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   634	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   635	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   636	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'

   645	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:410-449`, paper origin
   646	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   647	Its ambient coefficient vector is zero. -/
   648	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   649	  (.pauli W, 0)
   650	
   880	
   881	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   882	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:410-449`,
   883	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   884	-/
   885	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   886	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   887	  open Classical in
   888	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   889	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   890	      if tA = tB then
   891	        decide (a = b)
   892	      else
   893	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   894	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   895	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   896	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   897	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   898	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   899	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   900	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   901	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   902	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   903	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   904	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   905	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   906	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   907	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   908	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   909	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   910	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   911	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   912	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   913	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   914	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   915	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   916	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   917	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   918	          else true
   919	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   920	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   921	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   922	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   923	          else true
   924	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   925	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   926	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   927	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   928	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   929	    else false
   930	
   931	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   932	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   933	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:350-449`, paper origin
   934	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   935	-/
   936	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   937	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   938	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   939	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   940	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   941	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   942	  μ_prob := by
   943	    classical
   944	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   945	    exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   946	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P)) _
   947	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   948	
   949	end
   950	
   951	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Canonical Pauli basis test parameters
     5	
     6	This file defines the canonical admissible parameter tuple as a function of
     7	the target register size and states its quantitative soundness estimate.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The definitions and estimate correspond to `def:introparams` and
    12	`lem:delta-bound` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:534-555`, from
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1503-1562`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	noncomputable section
    20	
    21	/-- The admissibility predicate for a parameter tuple `(q, m, d)`. -/
    22	def IsAdmissibleTuple (t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) : Prop :=
    23	  IsAdmissibleSize t.1 ∧ 1 ≤ t.2.1 ∧ 1 ≤ t.2.2 ∧ t.2.1 ∣ t.1
    24	
    25	/-- Convert an admissible tuple to the parameter structure used by the
    26	Pauli basis game. -/
    27	def AdmissibleParams.ofTuple (t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)
    28	    (h : IsAdmissibleTuple t) : AdmissibleParams where
    29	  q := t.1
    30	  m := t.2.1
    31	  d := t.2.2
    32	  hd := h.2.2.1
    33	  hq := h.1
    34	  hdvd := h.2.2.2
    35	
    36	/-- The smallest even natural number represented by the ceiling prescription
    37	in `def:introparams`. -/
    38	noncomputable def introParamsC (a b : ℝ) : ℕ :=
    39	  2 * ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊
    40	
    41	/-- The canonical `(q, m, d)` tuple of `def:introparams`. -/
    42	def introParamsTuple (c R : ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ :=
    43	  (2 ^ (c * Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) + 1),
    44	    2 ^ Nat.log 2 (c * Nat.clog 2 R + 1), 1)
    45	
    46	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a numerical comparison of the two exponents
    47	appearing in the canonical tuple.  If `s` is positive and `r` is at most
    48	`2 ^ s`, then the base-two logarithm of `c * r + 1` does not exceed
    49	`c * s + 1`. -/
    50	private theorem log_two_le_mul_add_one (c r s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
    51	    (hrs : r ≤ 2 ^ s) : Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ c * s + 1 := by
    52	  have hkey : c * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ (c * s + 1) := by
    53	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos c with hc | hc
    54	    · subst hc
    55	      simp
    56	    · obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ : ∃ d, c = d + 1 := ⟨c - 1, by omega⟩
    57	      have h1 : d + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
    58	      have h2 : (d + 1) * r ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := Nat.mul_le_mul h1 hrs
    59	      have h3 : 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    60	        have hp : 0 < 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by positivity
    61	        omega
    62	      have h4 : 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) = 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    63	        rw [pow_add, pow_succ]
    64	        ring
    65	      have h5 : d + 1 + s ≤ (d + 1) * s + 1 := by
    66	        have hds : d ≤ d * s := by
    67	          simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul (le_refl d) hs
    68	        have hexp : (d + 1) * s = d * s + s := by ring
    69	        omega
    70	      calc (d + 1) * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s :=
    71	            Nat.add_le_add h2 h3
    72	        _ = 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) := h4.symm
    73	        _ ≤ 2 ^ ((d + 1) * s + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) h5
    74	  calc Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ Nat.log 2 (2 ^ (c * s + 1)) :=
    75	        Nat.log_mono_right hkey
    76	    _ = c * s + 1 := Nat.log_pow (by norm_num) _
    77	
    78	/-- The canonical tuple is admissible. This is the numerical
    79	admissibility part of `lem:delta-bound`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:547-555`, paper
    81	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1520-1562`. -/
    82	theorem introParamsTuple_isAdmissible (a b : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
    83	    IsAdmissibleTuple (introParamsTuple (introParamsC a b) R) := by
    84	  have hEven : Even (introParamsC a b) := ⟨⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊, two_mul _⟩
    85	  have hpow : Nat.clog 2 (2 ^ 2) ≤ Nat.clog 2 R :=
    86	    Nat.clog_mono_right 2 (by simpa using hR)
    87	  have hr2 : 2 ≤ Nat.clog 2 R := by
    88	    rwa [Nat.clog_pow 2 2 (by norm_num)] at hpow
    89	  have hs1 : 1 ≤ Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) := Nat.clog_pos (by norm_num) hr2
    90	  have hrs : Nat.clog 2 R ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) :=
    91	    Nat.le_pow_clog (by norm_num) _
    92	  exact ⟨⟨introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) + 1,
    93	      (hEven.mul_right _).add_one, rfl⟩,
    94	    Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by norm_num), le_rfl,
    95	    pow_dvd_pow 2 (log_two_le_mul_add_one _ _ _ hs1 hrs)⟩
    96	
    97	/-- The canonical admissible parameter structure of `def:introparams`,
    98	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:534-545`, paper
    99	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1503-1514`. -/
   100	noncomputable def introParams (a b : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
   101	    AdmissibleParams :=
   102	  AdmissibleParams.ofTuple _ (introParamsTuple_isAdmissible a b R hR)
   103	
   104	/-- The canonical parameter dimension supplies at least `R` encoded
   105	coordinates, as asserted in `lem:delta-bound`. -/
   106	theorem le_two_pow_introParams_m (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 0 < b)
   107	    (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
   108	    R ≤ 2 ^ (introParams a b R hR).m := by
   109	  have hc2 : 2 ≤ introParamsC a b := by
   110	    have hceil : 0 < ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊ :=
   111	      Nat.ceil_pos.mpr (div_pos (by linarith) (by linarith))
   112	    show 2 ≤ 2 * ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊
   113	    omega
   114	  have hlt : introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1 <
   115	      2 ^ Nat.log 2 (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1) * 2 := by
   116	    simpa [pow_succ] using
   117	      Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self (b := 2) (by norm_num)
   118	        (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1)
   119	  have hmul : 2 * Nat.clog 2 R ≤ introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R :=
   120	    Nat.mul_le_mul hc2 (le_refl _)
   121	  have key : Nat.clog 2 R ≤
   122	      2 ^ Nat.log 2 (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1) := by
   123	    omega
   124	  calc R ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 R := Nat.le_pow_clog (by norm_num) R
   125	    _ ≤ 2 ^ (2 ^ Nat.log 2 (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1)) :=
   126	        Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) key
   127	    _ = 2 ^ (introParams a b R hR).m := rfl
   128	
   129	/-- `lem:delta-bound`: the Pauli soundness error at the canonical parameters
   130	has polylogarithmic dependence on `R`. Blueprint
   131	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:547-555`, paper
   132	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1520-1562`.
   133	
   134	The explicit nonnegativity premise records the failure-probability domain
   135	inherited from `thm:pauli`; fractional powers of a negative real do not express
   136	the source's error parameter.
   137	
   138	**Local fix:** The third error term is bounded directly using the lower bound
   139	on `m`, rather than the source's false intermediate comparison between the
   140	field exponent and `m`. This discrepancy is documented in issue #16 and
   141	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_delta-bound-exponent-comparison.tex`; see also
   142	`rem:delta-bound-exponent-comparison`. -/
   143	theorem exists_deltaQld_introParams_bound (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a)
   144	    (hb : 0 < b) (hb' : b < 1) :
   145	    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' ≤ 1 ∧
   146	      ∀ (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) (ε : ℝ),
   147	        0 ≤ ε → deltaQld a b ε (introParams a b R hR).m
   148	            (introParams a b R hR).d (introParams a b R hR).q ≤
   149	          a' * (Real.rpow (Real.logb 2 R) a' * Real.rpow ε b' +
   150	            Real.rpow (Real.logb 2 R) (-b')) := by
   151	  sorry
   152	
   153	end
   154	
   155	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    30	tracked by issue #180. Paper `references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
    31	theorem pauliQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    32	    pauliQuestionDistribution P =

    35	        simp [pauliEdges]) (pauliCL P) (pauliCL P) := by

    39	in `lem:pauli-completeness`. -/
    40	theorem pauliQuestionDistribution_symm (P : AdmissibleParams)
    41	    (x y : PauliQuestion P) :
    42	    (pauliQuestionDistribution P).weight (x, y) =
    43	      (pauliQuestionDistribution P).weight (y, x) := by
    44	  sorry
    45	
    46	/-- Symmetry of the Pauli decision predicate in the symmetric game appearing in
    47	`lem:pauli-completeness`. -/
    48	theorem pauliWinPredicate_symm (P : AdmissibleParams)
    49	    (x y : PauliQuestion P) (a b : PauliAnswer P) :

    53	/-- The symmetric presentation of the Pauli basis test. The field and basis
    54	are those fixed by `P.model`; no additional model is quantified. -/
    55	noncomputable def pauliBasisTestSymm (P : AdmissibleParams) : SymmetricGame where
    56	  Question := PauliQuestion P

    60	  μ_symm := pauliQuestionDistribution_symm P
    61	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P

    64	/-- The symmetric presentation has the Pauli basis test as its

    66	theorem pauliBasisTestSymm_toGame (P : AdmissibleParams) :

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a conditionally linear syntax tree

+`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`,

+    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell

+      .succ (S₁.image f) (clReindexLinear hf L₁)
+        (by
+          intro x i hi
+          by_cases hex : ∃ k, f k = i
+          · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hex
+            have hk : k ∉ S₁ := fun hk => hi (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk)
+            show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) (f k) = 0
+            rw [clExtend_apply hf]
+            exact h _ k hk
+          · show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) i = 0
+            simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ hex])

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the transported syntax tree is supported on

+private theorem clReindexTerm_supportedOn {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
+    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (S : Finset κ)
+      (T : Finset ι), t.supportedOn S → S.image f ⊆ T →
+      (clReindexTerm hf t).supportedOn T := by
+  intro ell t
+  induction t with
+  | zero => intro S T _ _; trivial
+  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
+      intro S T hsupp hST
+      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hsupp
+      refine ⟨fun i hi => hST (Finset.image_subset_image h1 hi), fun y => ?_⟩
+      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_
+      intro i hi
+      obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
+      obtain ⟨hkS, hkS₁⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hk
+      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hST (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hkS), ?_⟩
+      intro hmem
+      obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
+      exact hkS₁ (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: evaluation commutes with the transport of a
+conditionally linear syntax tree along an injective reindexing. -/
+private theorem clReindexTerm_eval {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
+    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (x : ι → K),
+      CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf t) x =
+        clExtend f (CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun k => x (f k))) := by
+  intro ell t
+  induction t with
+  | zero => intro x; exact (clExtend_zero hf).symm
+  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
+      intro x
+      have hres : (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k)) =
+          coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)) := by
+        funext k
+        by_cases hk : k ∈ S₁
+        · have hmem : f k ∈ S₁.image f := Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk
+          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hmem]
+        · have hni : f k ∉ S₁.image f := by
+            intro hmem
+            obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
+            exact hk (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')
+          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hni]
+      have hhead : clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) =
+          clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))) := by
+        show clExtend f (L₁ (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k))) = _
+        rw [hres]
+      have hcomp : (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
+            (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)) =
+          L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) := by
+        rw [hhead]
+        exact clExtend_comp hf _
+      show clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) +
+          CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf (rest
+            (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
+              (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)))) x =
+        clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) +
+          CondLinearTerm.eval
+            (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))))
+            (fun k => x (f k)))
+      rw [hcomp, ih _ x, hhead, ← clExtend_add hf]
